moved.sentence: A recipe that claims `MUST display an error message on failure` when the source code makes no such attempt is a source fidelity failure regardless of whether the behavior is desirable.

judged.note: Rule must-not-claim-unattempted-error-handling turns the statement into an explicit MUST NOT and keeps the example claim, the condition (source makes no such attempt) and the clause that it is a source fidelity failure regardless of whether the behavior is desirable.

moved.sentence: Requirements derived from what "a well-implemented component would do" rather than what the code actually does are a source fidelity violation.

judged.note: Rule must-not-derive-requirements-from-an-ideal states it as a MUST NOT and keeps both the contrast (an ideal 'well-implemented component' versus what the code actually does) and the classification as a source fidelity violation.
